Distinguishing cellulitis from abscess

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 16-year-old has unilateral tonsillar inflammation but no obvious fluctuance. He is stable and can open his mouth. The clinician wants to distinguish peritonsillar cellulitis from a drainable abscess without routine CT exposure. Which test can help?

  1. Intraoral ultrasound
  2. Lateral soft-tissue neck radiography
  3. Noncontrast CT of the head
  4. Throat culture
  5. Serum inflammatory markers
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Intraoral ultrasound

Ultrasound can demonstrate a localized fluid pocket and help distinguish abscess from diffuse inflammation.

Understanding the options

Intraoral ultrasound
Ultrasound can demonstrate a localized fluid pocket and help distinguish abscess from diffuse inflammation.
Lateral soft-tissue neck radiography
This may assist in selected deep-neck questions but is less useful for distinguishing a local peritonsillar fluid collection from cellulitis.
Noncontrast CT of the head
Head CT does not adequately target the peritonsillar space or characterize this suspected collection.
Throat culture
A culture may identify organisms but does not show whether pus has formed a drainable pocket.
Serum inflammatory markers
Inflammatory markers cannot reliably distinguish cellulitis from a local abscess.
